def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Repeating separator lattice: each output cell corresponds to one tile.
    interior = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row),
                   key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h) if any(v != interior for v in grid[r])]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w) if any(grid[r][c] != interior for r in range(h))]

    # Keep the regularly spaced separator rows and columns.
    dr = min(b-a for a, b in zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:]))
    dc = min(b-a for a, b in zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:]))
    row_lines = [r for r in row_lines if (r-row_lines[0]) % dr == 0]
    col_lines = [c for c in col_lines if (c-col_lines[0]) % dc == 0]

    # Most separator intersections are the background; colored intersections
    # encode output cells. Map the intersection grid, treating the tile color
    # as the default and retaining only isolated markers.
    vals = [[grid[r][c] for c in col_lines] for r in row_lines]
    bg = max(set(v for row in vals for v in row),
             key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in vals))
    out = []
    for i in range(len(row_lines)-1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(col_lines)-1):
            v = vals[i][j]
            # A marker pair along a separator represents a single marker,
            # at the first position of the pair.
            if v == bg:
                row.append(interior)
            else:
                row.append(v)
        out.append(row)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter

    # Tile fill is the dominant color; separators form a regular lattice.
    counts = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row)
    fill = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Find separator rows and columns as those largely not filled with the tile color.
    rs = [r for r in range(h) if sum(x != fill for x in grid[r]) > w // 2]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] != fill for r in range(h)) > h // 2]

    def regular(lines):
        gaps = [b-a for a, b in zip(lines, lines[1:])]
        step = min(gaps)
        return [x for x in lines if (x-lines[0]) % step == 0]

    rs, cs = regular(rs), regular(cs)
    nr, nc = len(rs)-1, len(cs)-1

    # Each output cell is represented by the separator-junction color.
    # Use junctions at the upper/left edges, where the marker patterns are placed.
    out = [[fill for _ in range(nc)] for _ in range(nr)]
    for i in range(nr):
        for j in range(nc):
            v = grid[rs[i]][cs[j]]
            if v != fill:
                out[i][j] = v

    # Markers can also sit along the outermost boundary; these encode the
    # final row/column positions in the same lattice.
    for i in range(nr):
        for j in range(nc):
            candidates = [grid[rs[i]][cs[j]],
                          grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j]],
                          grid[rs[i]][cs[j+1]],
                          grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j+1]]]
            for v in candidates:
                if v != fill:
                    out[i][j] = v
                    break
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # The dominant color fills the repeated interior tiles.
    from collections import Counter
    interior = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Locate separator rows and columns, then use their regularly spaced
    # intersections as the encoded color sequence.
    rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v != interior for v in grid[r]) > w // 2]
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] != interior for r in range(h)) > h // 2]

    def regular(lines):
        step = min(b - a for a, b in zip(lines, lines[1:]))
        return [x for x in lines if (x - lines[0]) % step == 0]

    rows, cols = regular(rows), regular(cols)

    intersections = [[grid[r][c] for c in cols] for r in rows]
    background = Counter(v for row in intersections for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            a, b = intersections[i][j], intersections[i][j + 1]
            row.append(a if a == b and a != background else interior)
        out.append(row)
    return out
